claim: Sweeppea is a sweepstakes administration company offering full-service administration (starting at $2,999 per sweepstakes + $399/month platform fee) and a self-service SaaS platform ($99-$399/month), plus a $29/month Shopify buy-to-enter app.
notes: Corroborated by homepage; pricing fully public.

claim: Founded 2010 in Coral Gables, FL; two named principals (Marcos Menendez CEO, Martin Gaido CTO); claims clients including Coca-Cola, Honda, Yuengling, Tyson Foods, Wendy's, Budweiser, Chinet, ESPN; claims 'military-grade security (AWS infrastructure with SOC 2 compliance)' and '100% legal compliance in all 50 U.S. states'.
notes: Client list is marketing claim; SOC 2 wording attributes compliance to AWS infrastructure, not clearly to Sweeppea's own attestation.

claim: Third-party directories (ZoomInfo/RocketReach) estimate Sweeppea at roughly 3 employees and ~$3M revenue.
page_title: Sweeppea - Overview, News & Similar companies | ZoomInfo.com
notes: Directory estimates via search snippets; consistent with 2-founder team page. Treat as order-of-magnitude only.

claim: Full sweepstakes lifecycle is manageable programmatically via REST API v3: /sweepstakes/create, /clone, /fetch, /update, /delete, /pause, /unpause, with auto-generated entry pages.
notes: Sweepstakes creation is the core product across UI, API, CLI, and MCP.

claim: Official rules generation is productized: /rules/create, /rules/createWizard (14-step wizard) auto-inserts 'No Purchase Necessary', 'Void Where Prohibited', tax disclosures, and AMOE language; primary rules display on entry pages; AI-powered rules analysis advertised.
notes: Docs state every US sweepstakes 'must have Official Rules' and agents 'must never compose legal text' manually.

claim: Human legal-administration service: 'Advice to create legally compliant sweepstakes', drafting of Official Rules and Abbreviated Rules, and review of all ad materials for regulatory compliance; they 'work with legal professionals'.
notes: Service (human) capability, not software. Whether reviewers are licensed attorneys is not stated.

claim: AMOE is a first-class platform concept: dedicated 'ParticipantsAmoe' participant collection in the API, ActivateAmoeSwitch entry setting 'Required when any entry method involves a purchase, donation, or subscription', auto-generated AMOE language, mail-in entry handling in full service, and 'equal dignity' (identical entry quantities) validation.
page_title: Sweeppea MCP Documentation - Legal Compliance Guide
notes: Corroborated by OpenAPI Collection enum [Participants, ParticipantsAmoe, OptOuts] and entry-page tools doc.

claim: Entry management API: /participants/add (custom form fields, bonus entries, source attribution), /fetch with pagination/search/date filters, /count by collection, /single lookup by token/email/phone, /delete; participant groups; opt-out and AMOE collections; phone normalized to 10 digits (US/Canada).
notes: Entry state (entries, bonus entries, collections, groups) is per-sweepstakes, not a general customer-state store.

claim: Winner drawing API: POST /winners/draw performs weighted random selection ('participants with more bonus entries have a proportionally higher chance'), with eligibility filters (group, completed entries, opt-outs, spam exclusion); scheduled drawings support recurrence (hourly/daily/weekly/monthly); draws are blocked unless Official Rules exist.
notes: Winner tools doc contains no language on drawing certification, immutability, timestamps, or retention despite marketing 'certified drawing' claims (see SWEEPPEA-029).

claim: Full-service prize fulfillment: 'purchase, pack and ship winner prizes', digital gift card and promo code fulfillment, travel fulfillment, insured prizes.
notes: Human service in full-service tier, not self-service software.

claim: Winner tax workflows: 1099 & 1096 IRS form preparation, winner affidavits of eligibility, publicity/liability releases, and 'secure storage of SSN/Tax ID info for 1099-MISC issuance' for prizes over reporting thresholds.
page_title: Sweepstakes API for SaaS Platforms - Sweeppea
notes: Corroborated by full-service page ('1099 & 1096 IRS Forms') and pricing page (1099 MISC for prizes over $600); glossary states 1099-MISC at $2,000+, an internal inconsistency in threshold wording.

claim: Jurisdiction-specific compliance is encoded in the rules wizard and compliance guide: states parameter options that exclude FL/NY/RI 'to avoid registration requirements'; FL registration >$5,000 ARV filed >=7 days before start; NY >$5,000 filed >=30 days; RI >$500 for retailers with store-visit entry; Canada math skill-testing question; Quebec RACJ registration + French translation; 7 states (AL, IN, ME, MD, NC, VT, WV) require State Alcohol Board approval.
page_title: Sweeppea MCP Documentation - Legal Compliance Guide
notes: Encoded as wizard options, thresholds, and automatic warnings - template/checklist level, not versioned machine-readable law with provenance.

claim: Sweeppea performs 'Surety Bonds & State Registrations for FL, NY, and RI' and ABC approvals for alcohol sponsors as part of full-service administration.
notes: Also supports C01/C08 partial credit; a human filing service, not software workflow.

claim: The MCP server enforces synchronous server-side validations: 'If a call violates a rule, the tool is rejected and never reaches the Sweeppea API - no resources are created.' Two layers: hardcoded legal guardrails (blocking illegal lotteries without AMOE, COPPA under-13 refusal, alcohol age gates) described as inviolable, plus 'dynamic declarative rules' editable by Sweeppea applied to create_sweepstakes, update_entry_settings, create_rules_wizard, create_note, create_ticket, add_participant.
notes: Rules are vendor-managed (Sweeppea-editable), scoped to Sweeppea's own platform operations; customers cannot author or version these rules.

claim: Validation rejections return a structured payload 'so your AI assistant can recover', with fields blocked_by, error_code, error_message, and rule_id (rule_id present only for dynamic rules).
notes: Reason-coded deny exists but only for platform-management tool calls; no allow/deny/review model for customer product actions.

claim: Sweeppea MCP Server v1.19.0 exposes 83 tools in 18 categories (account, sweepstakes, participants, entry page, groups, notes, calendar, rules, billing/wallet, tickets, winners, documentation, utilities, to-do, testing, files, invoices, surveys) at https://mcp.sweeppea.com/ over MCP protocol 2025-11-25 (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0, bearer auth).
notes: Positioned as the industry's first sweepstakes MCP/AI-agent integration (about-us claim).

claim: Public REST API v3 (base https://api-v3.sweeppea.com) documented as an OpenAPI 3.1 spec with bearer-token auth and ~55 endpoints across account, entry page, sweepstakes, participants, groups, winners, rules, notes, calendar, billing, wallet, invoices, surveys, support, and tools/data; standard Response/Message/Data envelope and generic ErrorResponse.
notes: The API surface is fully enumerated in the spec: there are NO decision/authorization endpoints, no policy engine, no simulation, no decision-log endpoints. Used as positive evidence of absence for several 0 scores.

claim: Developer tooling: Sweeppea CLI (single native Rust binary via npm @sweeppea/cli) with OS-keyring auth, full --json output for scripting/CI-CD, confirmation prompts with --yes bypass; plus n8n nodes, Zapier (7,000+ apps), Klaviyo, Shopify app, ChatGPT App (OpenAI Apps SDK), and Agent Zero plugin. No conventional language SDKs (JS/Python libraries) are published.
notes: GitHub org Sweeppea-Development-Lab hosts mcp-info, mcp-documentation, api-documentation, n8n nodes, Agent Zero plugin.

claim: Webhooks are claimed on marketing pages ('The API includes real-time webhooks'; 'Set up real-time Webhooks for status updates (e.g., Winner Confirmed, Rules Updated)') but no webhook endpoints, event catalog, or subscription mechanism appears in the OpenAPI spec or API reference.
notes: Marketing-vs-docs discrepancy; scored 1 due to undocumented implementation.

claim: A sandbox is claimed on the SaaS API marketing page ('Utilize the Sandbox environment to test sweepstakes creation and participant injection without affecting live production data or billing') but no sandbox base URL, test keys, or sandbox section exists in the API reference.
page_title: Sweepstakes API for SaaS Platforms - Sweeppea
notes: Marketing-vs-docs discrepancy; scored 1.

claim: Geographic controls: 'IP blocking and geolocation restrictions' and 'geographic targeting'; the GeoLocation entry setting applies to 'GPS/IP-based geolocation detection. For physical location boundaries (e.g., store radius), NOT for state-level restrictions' - state-level eligibility is handled via the states parameter in rules creation (a legal-text restriction, not runtime blocking).
page_title: Sweeppea MCP Documentation - Entry Page Tools
notes: No compliance-grade geolocation (no VPN/proxy detection claims, no certainty scoring a la GeoComply).

claim: Age controls: min_age options 13+/18+/21+ in rules wizard; ActivateAgeGateSwitch 'ONLY activate when min_age is 21+ (alcohol/cannabis). NEVER activate for 18+ or 13+ promotions'; under-13 promotions refused outright (COPPA).
page_title: Sweeppea MCP Documentation - Entry Page Tools
notes: Age gate is self-certification level; no document-based or third-party age verification. SaaS API page tells platform customers to 'Implement front-end validation (Age Gate) before the API call'.

claim: Fraud/abuse controls: Cloudflare Turnstile bot protection, IP detection/blocking, automatic rate limiting and spam/bot filtering, 'Automatic identity, device, and information quality validation', 'Security filters and validation rules (powered with AI)', duplicate participation limits, mute/blacklist tools.
notes: Marketing-level description; spam flags surface in API (DoNotIncludeSpamParticipants draw filter) which corroborates spam classification existing in the data model.

claim: Winner-stage identity verification: 'Dedicated winner management app with biometric validation', 'Face recognition for winner verification', digital document signing, affidavits of eligibility.
notes: Applies to winner verification workflow only, not entry-time identity verification; no vendor named, no API exposure found.

claim: Named case studies/clients: Coca-Cola (Magic Summer sweepstakes), Tyson Foods ('over 30,000 entries'), Ensueno Fabric Softener, San Juan Seltzer (text-to-win), United Association (nonprofit donation entries), DiamondBack Covers (purchase-to-enter); legacy site adds Honda, Yuengling, Budweiser, Coors Light, Seagram's, Absolut, Sara Lee, Wendy's, Post, Warner Bros.
notes: Engagements appear to be per-campaign administration services, not deep platform integrations.

claim: Fully public pricing including an Enterprise tier (custom pricing, 20 sweepstakes, API access, 'Sweepstakes Compliance Review Services', dedicated account manager, bulk data import/export, enterprise-grade security language, AI assistants, 40 GB bandwidth).
notes: Rare transparency for the category; Enterprise 'Compliance Review Services' is a human review service.

claim: Sweeppea explicitly markets 'Compliance-as-a-Service: Powering Platform-Based Sweepstakes' for SaaS platforms embedding sweepstakes via API: 'Sweeppea assumes the role of the Independent Administrator, which is a critical legal shield during audits or state inquiries' and 'The platform is insulated from liability for the legal validity of the promotion.'
page_title: Sweepstakes API for SaaS Platforms - Sweeppea
notes: Exact quotes captured verbatim. This is the 'Compliance-as-a-Service' referenced in the core research question: liability outsourcing via third-party administration + rules generation + certified draws, NOT a policy/decisioning layer.

claim: Division of labor in the Compliance-as-a-Service model leaves runtime eligibility enforcement to the customer: 'Implement front-end validation (Age Gate) before the API call to ensure compliance with COPPA and state-specific eligibility' - i.e., Sweeppea does not authorize end-user actions in real time; platforms handle front-end age/geo validation and fraud prevention themselves.
page_title: Sweepstakes API for SaaS Platforms - Sweeppea
notes: Direct evidence AGAINST reading Sweeppea as a runtime authorization service; supports low J05/B03 scores.

claim: Audit-oriented claims: 'Maintaining auditable records of participant data and winner selections' (MCP README); 'Fetch and store the drawing certification details via GET /winners to provide to the user if their campaign is ever audited' (SaaS page); 'defensible one-click winner draws' with logged records (Shopify page). However, the winner tools reference documents no certification schema, immutability, or retention mechanics.
notes: Mixed evidence: audit records exist at the level of participant/winner data; no evidence of decision-grade reconstruction (inputs + rule version + output + approvals).

claim: Security posture per official Security Outline: HTTPS everywhere, encrypted backups (some active database data NOT encrypted at rest), daily multi-location backups, 2FA, dedicated network with firewalls/DDOS protection, AWS media storage, IP blocking, Cloudflare Turnstile, automatic rate limiting; 72-hour data deletion window after account closure. Features page adds 'SOC 2 Type II compliance for enterprise custom development' and '99.9% uptime guarantee' - no SOC 2 attestation, ISO 27001, pen-test report, or formal SLA document was found.
notes: SOC 2 wording is scoped ('for enterprise custom development') and about-us attributes SOC 2 to AWS infrastructure - ambiguous whether Sweeppea itself holds a SOC 2 report. Trust Center page content could not be retrieved (fetches resolved to other pages).

claim: Data retention: 'All participants data deleted within 72 hours after the customer's account is closed'; deletion/anonymization on request unless legally required to retain; GDPR roles (controller for accounts, processor for participant data); SCCs for international transfer.
notes: Fixed policy, not customer-configurable retention controls.

claim: Wallet endpoints (/wallet/fetch, /wallet/deposit, /wallet/withdraw) are ACCOUNT-level funds for platform billing, and the Non-Profit plan's 'donation wallet and fund tracking' tracks donations - there is no end-user/participant wallet, credit ledger, or entitlement system.
notes: Basis for low F-category scores; the only user-level 'balance' is entry counts per sweepstakes.

claim: Sweeppea's own comparison page positions it against Woobox, ShortStack, and ViralSweep, claiming differentiation on 'Legal Compliance & Admin' focus: independent third-party administrator role, automatic NY/FL bonding, 1099-MISC handling, ABC alcohol approvals, purchase-to-enter, AMOE management, affidavits.
page_title: Comparison: Sweeppea vs Woobox vs ShortStack vs ViralSweep
notes: Self-serving comparison but useful for competitive mapping; confirms compliance administration is the differentiator, not decisioning tech.

claim: Adjacent full-service administration substitutes exist: Marden-Kane (sweepstakes administration since 1957), National Sweepstakes Company (structures promotions to comply with promotional law, originates official rules, bonds and registers with applicable states), US Sweepstakes & Fulfillment Co. (SMS/text promotions), Odds On Promotions, and randomdraws.com (certified random prize draws).
page_title: Marden-Kane, Inc. + National Sweepstakes Company + ussweeps.com (via search)
notes: Confirms the sweepstakes-administration service category is crowded with human-service incumbents that absorb compliance liability.

claim: Shopify buy-to-enter app converts purchases to entries in real time ('1 entry per $1 spent'; 'Purchase activity becomes entries immediately, with no added checkout friction'), automatically provides a compliant free entry form (AMOE), and includes rules generation and audit-trailed draws.
page_title: Sweeppea Made for Shopify - Buy-to-Enter Sweepstakes
notes: Closest thing to event-driven entry ingestion; still campaign entry accrual, not decisioning.

claim: No customer-facing regulatory change monitoring product exists; regulatory knowledge is maintained by Sweeppea itself via annually-updated guides ('How to Run a Legal Sweepstakes 2026'), a static 50-state/DC law guide, a compliance glossary, and vendor-editable dynamic declarative rules in the MCP validation layer.
page_title: Sweepstakes and Contest Laws by State - Sweeppea
notes: Inference from enumerated product surface: change monitoring happens inside Sweeppea's ops, not as a product feature customers can subscribe to.

claim: The commercial model is 'Human Expert + Platform': full-service (expert creates and manages sweepstakes) is the flagship; bonding/registration, ABC approvals, legal review, 1099s, and Enterprise 'Sweepstakes Compliance Review Services' all depend on Sweeppea staff; platform training offered ($750 on Self-Service tier).
notes: Compliance outcomes are delivered substantially by professional services, with software as workflow support.

claim: Text-to-win entry via short code 65047 with sweepkeys; Sweeppea publishes TCPA compliance guidance (opt-in disclosure language, STOP/HELP opt-out, 8am-9pm quiet hours, Mobile Marketing Association best practices) for SMS sweepstakes entries.
page_title: Sweeppea Blog - Text to Win / TCPA compliance articles
notes: Entry-method-specific (SMS) legal handling embedded in operations and educational content.

claim: The API reference contains no sections on webhooks, sandbox, API versioning policy, idempotency keys, rate limit quotas, request logs, or an error-code catalog; versioning exists only as the v3 base URL; error responses are a generic {Response:false, Message} envelope.
notes: Positive evidence of absence for developer-platform maturity squares (H03-H07); MCP AI guide advises agents to self-throttle ('Rate limiting - batch information gathering'), implying limits exist but are undocumented.

claim: POST /participants/add functions as an entry-event ingestion API (lang, source, sweepstakesToken, entryPageFields with custom Fields and BonusEntries), supporting 'entries-per-dollar' real-time synchronization from external platforms.
notes: Single-purpose ingestion (sweepstakes entries), not a generic event/action decision API; response is success/error, not allow/deny/review with obligations.

claim: Legacy site offers 'Expert administration of contests, sweepstakes and game promotions' including contests with 'Expert judging, planning, compliance' - contest/skill-judging is a human service; the self-service platform and API are sweepstakes-centric (random drawing), with no contest-judging or instant-win game engine documented.
page_title: Contest & Sweepstakes Company Full Administration - Sweeppea
notes: Scheduled recurring drawings (hourly/daily) exist but are not instant-win mechanics.

claim: Agency model: Sweeppea acts as 'a silent compliance partner, handling state bonding, legal rules drafting, and winner management'; an account manager can 'oversee 10 different client sweepstakes from a single dashboard - monitoring entries, winner status, and compliance for every active promotion simultaneously' ('Sweepstakes-as-a-Service').
notes: Multi-client/multi-campaign management exists; no evidence of formal multi-tenant org hierarchy, per-brand RBAC, or SSO.

claim: Sweeppea publishes a static educational state-by-state guide covering all 50 states + DC (registration/bonding thresholds, Material Element Test vs Dominant Factor Doctrine, prize/chance/consideration lottery elements), plus a compliance glossary defining AMOE, bonding, ARV, consideration, equal dignity, COPPA, 1099-MISC.
page_title: Sweepstakes and Contest Laws by State - Sweeppea
notes: Educational content citing legal concepts; generated rules documents do not carry machine-readable legal-source provenance.
